newsitem.title: USA: Trans World Gaming unit sues Louisiana.
newsitem.headline: Trans World Gaming unit sues Louisiana.

text.p: Trans World Gaming Corp on Tuesday said that one of its subsidiaries filed a lawsuit against the state of Louisiana, contending its constitutional rights were violated when it was prevented from advertising its views on a ballot question regarding video poker.

In the suit, the company's Chrysolith LLC unit, a licensed video poker operator, contends it was barred from promoting its support for the proposition, while opponents were not barred from advertising.
Eventually, after a petition and a state Supreme Court ruling, the company was allowed to advertise its position on the ballot question 17 days prior to the vote, it said.
The proposition asked voters in November, on a parish-by-parish basis, if video poker should be allowed. The measure passed in some parishes, or counties, and was rejected in others.
